newsitem.title: THAILAND: Amnuay says central bank not propping up baht.
newsitem.headline: Amnuay says central bank not propping up baht.

text.p: Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan said on Friday the baht rallied against a weakening U.S. dollar in line with market forces and he believed the central bank had not intervened to artificially prop up the Thai unit.
Amnuay said the official baht/dollar midrate fixed by the Bank of Thailand at 25.99 on Friday, against 26.05 on Thursday, reflected the U.S. dollar's movement in major markets.
The minister told reporters: "I do not believe the central bank would take actions to resist market mechanism."

Currency dealers in Singapore said the Bank of Thailand intervened there on Friday morning by selling dollars at 26.025 baht after the Thai unit came under intense pressure on rumours it denied of a baht band widening.
Amnuay's remark followed an earlier repeated denial by central bank officials of rumours of a change in Thailand's exchange rate mechanism.
The central bank issued a statement late on Friday that the Thai economy was moving in the right direction with an improvement in price stability.
The baht was quoted at 25.975/26.025 to the dollar late on Friday.
